title: Joining Jeter-Pillars in St. Louis; Harry Edison
summary: Dropped in St. Louis, he joined the Jeter-Pillars band at the Plantation Club, where Harry Edison, 17, was already playing.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So the band, they came back to Pittsburgh, and I went to St. Louis, as far as St. Louis with Mary. So Mary says, "Listen, Kenny --," Jeter - Wilbur Kirk was playing with this band, Jeeter Piller's band, in St. Louis, and they were working at the Plantation Club, you know, with Ziggy Johnson, these big shows and things, from Chicago, you know.
Yeah.

So he said -- Mary Lou says, "Well, all those shows, you played all those big time acts in the Cotton Club. I know you could make this gig." So I said, "Well, Mary --," I was kind of scared, because the Plantation was a big club at that time.
Yeah.

So anyway, Wilbur Kirk, he was so wonderful, you know, said, "Well, come on, Kenny, try." So there was Harry Edison, who was 17 years old at the time, and when I left to go I took him with me, and his mother said -- he's from Columbus, Ohio. So his mother says, "Kenny, look out for
Harry, because I was a little older than Harry." So I said, "Well, don't worry, Mrs. Edison."
Well, in other words, Harry was in that Leroy Bradley band?
No, no.
Oh, you just knew him.
Just knew him from Columbus, Columbus, Ohio, which is about -- oh, I don't know, about 30 miles from Cincinnati.
[End of Side 2]
-- Harry already blowing then?
Yeah, he was a wonderful trumpet player.
That early, huh?
Yeah, but he never got around to, you know, playing with any name --
Did he always have a new concept, (unintelligible) like he showed himself to have when he went to England?
Oh, yeah. When we played together in St. Louis, he was so wonderful.
Was he.
So we joined the band -- No, I think Harry was in the band, I guess, oh, maybe a couple of days before I was. I joined the band.
Now, wait a minute. I'm muddled. Because we started to say that Mary said to you, "You can play
that Plantation."

Yeah. But see, Harry left. When we left Columbus, Harry went straight to join the Jeter-Pillar's band, and I stayed with Mary Lou Williams for awhile and then we drove out. See, that was the thing, because Harry was there.
So Harry was there.
Harry was there when I got there. Harry was there.
Oh, I see.
And --
In Columbus.
In Columbus. So he -- immediately he was my roommate, because I found him right away.
Yeah, right.
So --
So, I mean then Jeter-Pillars just invited you to join the band?
Join the band. I joined the band right away.
